key_insight: R3D finds that the chief barriers to 3D policy learning are missing 3D data augmentation and harmful interactions with Batch Normalization; by combining a scalable transformer-based 3D encoder with a diffusion decoder and targeted training fixes, stable training and strong generalization become possible.
problem_solved: Addresses training instability and severe overfitting that prevented adoption of powerful 3D perception models for policy learning and cross-embodiment transfer.
method: Systematic diagnosis pinpointing two root causes: absence of 3D data augmentation and adverse effects of Batch Normalization on policies.
New architecture: scalable transformer-based 3D encoder coupled with a diffusion decoder, together with BatchNorm removal/replacement and 3D-specific augmentation recipes.
Training protocol and regularization (3D augmentations, normalization fixes) to stabilize learning and reduce overfitting, enabling cross-embodiment transfer.
impact: Provides practical fixes and an architecture that let practitioners safely scale 3D perception models in policy learning, improving robustness, generalization, and transfer across robot embodiments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: 3D input -> transformer 3D encoder -> diffusion decoder -> policy output (show data-flow and training signals).
Before/after bar or line chart: metrics (overfitting gap, validation performance) comparing baseline vs R3D.
Augmentation collage: visual icons/examples of 3D augmentations (rotation, scaling, point jittering) with brief captions.
Normalization effect plot: training loss/validation curves illustrating instability with BatchNorm vs stable training after replacement.
paper_authors: Zhengdong Hong, Shenrui Wu, Haozhe Cui, Boyi Zhao, Ran Ji
